sample_size.quote:
We can thus use 1,871 observations in tests of client
importance at the audit firm level. Zip codes of client firm headquarters, required for
distance-based matching with audit offices, are unavailable for another 93 firms (in most
cases because the headquarters are in foreign countries, e.g., Bermuda), so we have a sample
of 1,778 observations for tests of client importance at the local-audit-office level.

sample_unit.quote:
Our 1,871 sample firms belong to 54 different industries (two-digit SIC codes). Table
2 presents descriptive statistics for the 1,871 sample firms on the variables used in subsequent regressions.

sample_period.quote:
Our sample consists of all companies that reveal audit and nonaudit fees in proxy statements
filed between February 5 and June 30, 2001, have data on Compustat, and meet certain
criteria (such as being clients of Big 5 audit firms, and not having changed auditors during
2000, n - 1,871).

III. DATA AND DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
We collect from proxy statements information on audit, IT, and other fees paid by
companies to their auditors. Disclosure was required in proxy statements beginning February 5, 2001. Because the SEC Final Rule (SEC 2000) requires proxy statements to disclose ‘‘financial information systems design and implementation fees,’’ we searched the 10K Wizard (http:/ /www.10kwizard.com) for proxy statements filed between February 5 and
